description: Zero claims extracted but reconciliation status returned CLEAN
root_cause: No rule tested for an empty claim list; every other rule is vacuously silent with no rows, so an unread table exported a green badge

description: 0 claims extracted from a 5-page document holding 12
root_cause: pdfplumber ruled detection returned the boxed header block as the table: a header, one row (the third header line) and none of the claim data, which sits below the ruling. Nothing checked that the chosen table contained data.

description: Claim # / OneClaim # mapped to nothing, so no claim-number column existed
root_cause: normalize_label stripped # entirely, leaving "claim oneclaim" with no token saying it is a number

description: Three columns labelled Total; Ind/BI and Alloc Exp unmapped
root_cause: Repeated parent labels are disambiguated only by the child row beneath them (Reserves/Recoveries/Incurred), and the trade abbreviations ind, bi, alloc were absent from the component vocabulary

description: 12 of 12 claims found but every date and money field null (24 R-07)
root_cause: Each claim is a three-line record whose fields are distributed across the lines: name on line A, identifier and status on line B, dates and money on line C. The header is three lines, one per record line. The engine models one header and one line per claim, so only line B survives and the rest folds into the description.

description: AIG-style identifier smearing rejected 8 of 12 legitimate claim ids
root_cause: The identifier-shape consensus introduced for Liberty rejected cells where a neighbouring column bled in, because the smeared cell has a different shape. A false negative created by a previous generalized fix.

description: A single-claim report extracted zero claims
root_cause: The recurrence floor required a shape to appear at least twice, so a shape appearing once -- an ordinary one-claim loss run -- was rejected entirely.

description: 162 rows extracted against a printed count of 28; 152 of them from inside the loss run pages
root_cause: Each claim is a stacked multi-line detail block. Continuation lines land in the claim-number column, and build_claim accepts any non-empty value there as a new claim. Continuation folding only fires when that cell is empty.

description: 10 further rows extracted from page 54, a financial statement outside the loss run, with claim_number '0'
root_cause: Extraction runs over every page of a compound document; no test that an identifier-shaped value is present

description: Loss run occupies pages 39-51 of a 99-page board packet; the other 86 pages are municipal meeting material
root_cause: No notion of which pages constitute the loss-run section of a compound document

description: 84 candidate rows with every date and money field null (168 R-07 findings)
root_cause: Not yet root-caused; row detection succeeds but field association fails

description: Carrier identified as 'Status Currency Indemnity'
root_cause: Letterhead detection picked a header fragment

description: 0 claims; no headers detected at all
root_cause: Not yet root-caused; combines scanned pages, Italian labels and EU numerics

description: 6 of 23 pages carry no text layer
root_cause: Vision path disabled in the cold run; OCR contribution not yet measured

description: Two columns, Total Incurred and Net Incurred, both mapped to incurred_total; the second was silently dropped and the document reported CLEAN
root_cause: map_headers demoted the losing column to unmapped and nothing downstream recorded that a materially distinct money column had been discarded. Arithmetic still balanced over the surviving values.

description: Three columns printed Total; two were discarded without trace
root_cause: Same mechanism. Disambiguated here by the child header row, but where that is absent the ambiguity must be preserved rather than resolved by guessing.

description: 12 claims extracted with every date and every amount null (24 R-07 errors); each claim occupies three printed lines and only the line carrying the identifier was read
root_cause: The engine modelled one header line and one line per claim. AIG heads its table with three lines of labels, one per line of a three-line record: claimant, then identifier and status, then dates and money. Reading line by line, the claim was built from the identifier line alone and the other two lines were folded into its description or warned about.

description: Money read one column left of where it belonged, so an amount printed under Ind/BI Paid arrived as Med/PD Paid
root_cause: Column boundaries were taken from the midpoints between header cells, but money prints right-aligned under a left-aligned label and sits past that midpoint. Invisible on page 2, where every amount is .00; on page 4 it would have moved 15,000.00 into medical.

description: Two R-01 errors reported against a carrier that had made none, totalling 41,880 and 2,403
root_cause: R-01 read an unprinted paid total as zero, and a first attempt at the fix summed whatever paid components happened to be present. CNA prints an Expenses Total this engine does not map, so the indemnity alone stood in for the paid figure and the unmapped expenses were reported as the carrier's arithmetic error.

description: claim_status reads UNKNOWN on 11 of 12 claims
root_cause: The status column is narrow and the loss description printed to its right bleeds into it, so the cell reads 'Closed INSD, IV DID NOT HIT OV. MORE DETAILS PENDING WITH' and the status vocabulary matches nothing. Predates F18 and is unchanged by it. Left open deliberately: closed once XL showed the same failure from a different cause -- there the claimant name runs into the status, here the description does. A cell whose first word is a status word states that status.

description: date_reported is null on every claim; the document prints a Receipt Date column
root_cause: 'Receipt Date' is not in the mapping vocabulary, so the column maps to nothing and its dates are dropped. Left open deliberately: worth generalising only once a second carrier shows the same gap.

description: 84 rows extracted with every date and both amounts null; 168 R-07 errors
root_cause: The heading wraps onto a second line BELOW the one that scores as the header, and the merge only looked upwards. Half the labels were never read, and the line itself was left in the body where its words close the gutters between the very columns it names.

description: Four columns collapsed into two: company with insured, and claim status with claimant and currency
root_cause: A gutter is space EVERY row leaves blank, so two claimant names long enough to touch the currency beside them, plus a footer set at its own positions, closed boundaries that eighty-two other rows agreed on. A column the header names twice is now cut where most of its rows leave a channel wider than the space they set between their own words.

description: Carrier reported as 'Status Currency Indemnity'
root_cause: The letterhead scan reads the top of page one, which on a spreadsheet export is the table's own heading. The company is printed as a column on every row instead, and a column naming a document-level fact is now read as one -- carrier, insured, policy, term and currency alike.

description: Both amounts landed in one cell under a single label; reserve and payment indistinguishable
root_cause: Money prints right-aligned under a left-aligned label, so 'Payment Indemnity' sat left of the amounts it heads and its first word landed in the column before. A header word now follows its own label rather than the nearest column edge.

description: Claim Status and Claimant Name arrive as one column: claimant_name reads 'Closed GIANCARLO DE ANGELIS'
root_cause: OPEN. The two columns are separated by 3.8pt and the words inside them by 3.86pt, so no geometric rule can part them without also cutting every prose column on every other document. The header names both. Recovering them needs a source column to be allowed to carry two canonical fields, which the mapping cannot yet express -- a schema/mapping coverage gap, not a parsing failure.

description: incurred_total null on all 84 claims, so every one fails R-07
root_cause: OPEN, and correct. The carrier prints a gross reserve and a payment and no incurred total. Deriving one would invent a figure the document never stated and make R-01 vacuous. The document is held for review because a required field is genuinely absent from the source.

description: 0 claims and R-20; the one English loss run in the packet came back as interleaved letters
root_cause: Page 19 is a wide carrier sheet fitted onto A4: 2.16pt glyphs, gutters under a point. Every geometry threshold was stated in absolute points -- the four-point floor on what counts as a column gutter, the four points of slack for a word sitting outside its column, and beneath them pdfplumber's own three-point word tolerance. At a fifth of ordinary scale each is several characters wide, so columns merged, lines merged, and a company and the programme name beside it came back as 'ComEpuarnoyp eSEan'. All three are now proportional to the page's own text.

description: Earned premium of 226,605.00 from a second loss run in the packet was checked against this run's 28 claims, reporting two R-04 errors of a quarter of a million
root_cause: Totals rows were ranked by how many amounts they carried, with no test of which claims they total. A 99-page board packet holds several loss runs; the widest totals row won regardless of whose it was. A totals row that names a claim count now has to name this run's count, and one naming a different count outranks nothing.

description: 6 of 23 pages carry no text layer and are not read
root_cause: OPEN. The vision path is disabled without an API key, so those pages contribute nothing and the document says so (the warning names the six pages). Unchanged by this work.

description: 13 of 23 pages are Italian-language loss runs from other insurers and yield nothing
root_cause: OPEN and out of scope. CLAUDE.md section 13 places non-English documents outside the product. The packet holds runs from UNIQA, Unipol, Lloyd's and others with Italian column labels (Data Sinistro, Riservato, Liquidato) and several print no claim number at all. Reading them needs a vocabulary decision, not a parsing fix.

description: Carrier reads 'CAMERA DI COMMERCIO DI TORINO', which is the insured
root_cause: OPEN and pre-existing, unchanged by this work. Page 1 of the packet is the insured's own Italian cover sheet, so the letterhead scan reads the insured's name. The English run on page 19 does print a Company Name column, but its text overprints the column beside it and the two merge, so the column-stated carrier is not available either.

description: R-01 reports a 2,000.00 discrepancy the carrier did not make
root_cause: OPEN. The row reads Payment 5,820.62, Receivable -2,000.00, Total Incurred 3,820.62 -- the carrier's arithmetic is right. The Receivable column is a recovery the vocabulary does not know, and it is printed negative, so mapping it needs a sign convention that two claims (one of them all zeros) cannot establish. Left unmapped and flagged rather than mapped on a guess.
